target: pappus element (PO_0025394); length (PATO_0000122) equal among the bristles
fix: 'Pappus ..., bristles subequal': the comparison is among the pappus bristles, so the part is the pappus element (pappus bristle is a synonym), not the whole pappus. 'Subequal' compares the bristles' lengths with each other.
reason: The bristles are what is subequal; PO has pappus element with the synonym pappus bristle.

fix: 'female sepals ...; male sepals ...': a sex qualifier before the part must fill the whole/state slot. Otherwise the taxon gets contradictory sepal descriptions.
reason: Only the female sepals are obtuse or acute; the male sepals are connate with obtuse-denticulate lobes.
The pappus bristles range from straw-coloured (yellow) to rufous (reddish orange). Reading it as a continuum on the pappus is right.
'Seasonally green' means losing leaves seasonally, i.e. deciduous. The two alternatives are evergreen or deciduous, as recorded.
The bracts are narrowly triangular or lanceolate. The degree word 'narrowly' is kept; 'linear' is the other end of the preceding 'to' range.
'Trees' means a tree (arborescent) habit.

fix: 'male flowering pedicel': the sex qualifier must fill the whole/state slot. The female pedicel is described separately in the same text.
reason: The 2 cm length applies only to male flowers' pedicels.

fix: 'Outer female florets ... whitish. Bisexual disk florets yellowish': both the position (outer) and the sex of the floret must be kept. Otherwise one flower gets both white and yellow.
reason: Only the outer female florets are whitish; the disk florets are yellowish.

fix: 'peduncle' was mapped to pedicel. Peduncle has its own PO class.
reason: The flora says the peduncles are short, not the pedicels.

fix: 'lowest bract ..., exceeding culm, the others reduced': a position word such as lowest/upper/outer must fill the position slot.
reason: Only the lowest bract exceeds the culm; the other bracts are reduced.
'Short-exserted' means exserted, only slightly. Exserted on the style is right.

fix: 'rounded to cuneate at the base' and '... at the apex': a trailing 'at the base/apex' moves the quality to the leaf base or apex, not the whole leaf.
reason: The rounded-to-cuneate range describes the leaf base.
The corolla opens fully but is not reflexed. A negated 'reflexed' on the corolla is right.

fix: 'obovate-lanceolate' is the standard compound for oblanceolate (lanceolate, widest above the middle). Where PATO has a single term for the hyphenated compound, use it instead of a continuum between its parts.
reason: PATO has oblanceolate; a continuum from obovate to lanceolate misreads the compound.
The floral bracts exceed (are longer than) the sepals.
The fruit body (as opposed to the wings) is sparsely pubescent to glabrous. Fruit is an acceptable part.
Each peduncle bears 3 to 7 flowers. The count of flowers inside the peduncle container is right.

fix: 'the three outer linear, the three inner linear-elliptic to oblanceolate': inner/outer must fill the position slot. Otherwise the lobes get both shapes.
reason: Only the inner three lobes have this shape; the outer three are linear.
The leaf blades become thick when old. Increased thickness with the 'old' context is right.

target: shape (PATO_0000052) only, or a crown-shape value (no suitable existing term)
fix: 'umbrella-like crown' (a spreading, flat-topped tree crown) must not map to umbelliform, which config/flopo_quality_bearer_constraints.tsv limits to inflorescences.
reason: Umbelliform is an inflorescence term; the flora is describing the shape of the tree's crown.
'Obovate-elliptic' is a shape between obovate and elliptic, so the continuum reading fits. It is one of three listed alternatives.
Ray florets are absent.
'Rhombic-ovate' is a shape between rhombic and ovate, so the continuum reading fits. Ovate uses the temporary FLOPO class.
The stems are 3-10 dm high, which is 30-100 cm.
7 to 11 secondary veins on each side of the midrib; the landmark (midrib) is recorded.
The plants (trees or shrubs) are 1 to 18 m tall.
The leaf margin is subrevolute, i.e. approximately revolute.
The shrubs are 30-100 dm tall, which is 300-1000 cm.
Each inflorescence has 13 to 18 flowers.
There are 20 stamens.
